subject: Evaluation temperature check + commitment fence for Cerulean go-live
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan.park@ceruleanhealth.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: program-team@ceruleanhealth.com
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation window — slight timeline pressure

Hi Logan / Camila,

Quick heads-up: during our environment soak this morning we found a regression in the nightly ingest step that pushes the acceptance window out by ~3 business days. The Cerulean ops team and I did a quick triage — looks like a config drift on our side but it does change the go-live target.

We know this is late in the schedule; we wanted to surface it early so we can align on contingency options (short-term mitigation vs. shift of final acceptance). Attached is a short log excerpt and our updated internal runbook.

Proposed immediate asks:
- Can Redwood lock the current evaluation model snapshot for a 72-hour window so we can do reproducible tests?
- Can you confirm whether the MAP milestones still map to the same sign-off owners if we move the acceptance date?

Thanks — Susan

Attachments: eval-test-plan-logs.pdf (excerpt), Cerulean internal runbook (ref)

From: logan_wright@redwood.ai
To: Susan Park <susan.park@ceruleanhealth.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation window — slight timeline pressure

Susan — thanks for the flag and the logs. Short answers: we can pin the model snapshot and freeze the test harness for 72 hours; Camila will confirm the snapshot id and update the MAP artifact.

Longer answer (quick plan):
1) Pin snapshot (72h) — Redwood will create a read-only snapshot and a short-lived test endpoint.
2) Quick triage call (30m) — propose Mon 10am PT to sync triage steps and ownership.
3) Commitment fence proposal: if Cerulean needs >72h, we will present a small schedule buffer proposal to execs (see attached CSV for cost/latency implications).

Camila — can you produce the snapshot id and list any downstream model variants we should lock? Hannah — flagging this for escalation if the buffer request grows beyond 1 week.

— Logan

Signature:
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachment: proposed-commitment-fence.csv (stub)

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Susan Park <susan.park@ceruleanhealth.com>, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Snapshot details + short checklist

Susan — pinned snapshot created: snapshot-ceru-20270503-09. Endpoint: https://test.redwood.internal/snapshots/snapshot-ceru-20270503-09 (read-only, 72h TTL).

Quick checklist we've attached to the MAP:
- Confirm ingestion fix (Cerulean)
- Run 2x nightly regeneration against pinned snapshot (Cerulean + Redwood)
- Validate SLA metrics: 95th latency under 1200ms, token accuracy passes regression suite
- Final sign-off owners: Susan (Cerulean PM), Paul Nguyen (Cerulean Ops), Logan (Redwood AE), Camila (Redwood Solutions)

If the regeneration fails twice, we recommend moving the acceptance gate by 3 business days OR triggering the contingency lane below.

Contingency lane (quick):
- Short-term: Redwood increases endpoint parallelism for 48h to absorb retries (cost uplift ~9%)
- Medium-term: schedule a 2-day evaluation extension and push the go/no-go decision to the exec sync (we'll need a formal buffer request)

I'll join Mon 10am for triage.

— Camila

Attachment: Cerulean_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP artifact)

From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@ceruleanhealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: Susan Park <susan.park@ceruleanhealth.com>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot details + short checklist

Thanks Camila — we ran the regeneration overnight against the pinned snapshot and the ingestion fix held. Two notes:
- We observed increased retry volume during the first pass; ops will re-run and sanity-check logs this morning.
- For governance we need a written commitment fence that specifies whether the 72h freeze holds the current MAP dates or allows a 3-day automatic extension if any verification tests fail twice.

Can Redwood draft the commitment fence language we can include as an addendum to the MAP? We want to avoid ambiguous ownership when we flip the acceptance date.

— Paul (Cerulean Ops)

Attachment: none

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@ceruleanhealth.com>, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Commitment fence draft (internal -> external proposal)

Paul / Susan — looping you in with a draft commitment fence. If Cerulean agrees we can append this to the MAP and circulate for signatures. Quick summary below; full text in body.

Draft commitment fence (summary):
- Redwood will pin snapshot snapshot-ceru-20270503-09 for 72 hours (start: 2027-05-03T09:00:00Z).
- If Cerulean verification fails twice during the 72h window, Redwood will provide a one-time 72h extension (i.e., total freeze up to 144h) subject to a buffer request filed to Redwood Sales Ops.
- Any extension beyond 144h requires a formal schedule rebaseline and Exec approval (redwood-sales-exec@redwood.ai).
- During any extension Redwood may enable temporary parallelism to reduce retries (estimated cost uplift included in attached CSV).

Full addendum (paste):
[BEGIN ADDENDUM]
Commitment Fence Addendum — Cerulean Health / Redwood Inference
1. Purpose: provide deterministic frozen test conditions to validate ingestion and regression tests without model drift.
2. Scope: snapshot-ceru-20270503-09 and the MAP artifact Cerulean_MAP_v2.xlsx.
3. Durations: 72h freeze; one discretionary 72h extension for repeated verification failures; any further extension requires rebaseline approval.
4. Owners & approvals: Cerulean PM (Susan Park) signs acceptance; Redwood AE (Logan Wright) requests buffer; Redwood Sales Ops approves short buffer; Exec approval for >144h.
5. Cost & trade-offs: temporary parallelism option (cost uplift ~9%) or scheduled extended test window (no uplift but requires rebaseline).
[END ADDENDUM]

Paul / Susan — if this aligns, reply with OK and we'll generate a signed addendum and a DocuSign link. Marissa — please stand by to escalate to Sales Ops if they request >144h.

— Hannah

Signature:
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Cloud Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Susan Park <susan.park@ceruleanhealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Cc: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@ceruleanhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commitment fence draft (internal -> external proposal)

Hannah — thank you. Cerulean accepts the draft addendum with one small change: the discretionary extension should be 48h (not 72h) because we want to limit drift to a single business day.

OK to proceed on that basis. Susan (PM) will sign the addendum once the DocuSign link is up; Paul confirms ops is green on the pinned runs and we will not request additional extensions unless a hard failure recurs.

Please send DocuSign and updated MAP artifact with the 48h change.

— Susan
